verdict.rationale: CMS IndusLaw publishes detailed, founder-facing analysis of Indian startup-specific rules: the 2026 Startup Notification covering recognition timelines, turnover thresholds and the deep-tech pathway, plus an ESOP stock-option tax publication on the Flipkart buyback ruling. This covers the Indian market well, but nothing in the evidence shows publications on other jurisdictions' instruments, and Indian FDI appears only on a practice page rather than in a publication. Missing for 10: publications on non-Indian instruments (UK EMI, German VSOP, French BSPCE), a dedicated Indian FDI publication for startups, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, the firm publishes on jurisdiction-specific startup instruments and rules of my market — e.g. UK EMI schemes, German VSOPs, Indian FDI/ESOP rules, French BSPCE

citations.quote: Deep tech startups enjoy an extended recognition period of twenty years from incorporation or registration
The Tribunal further held that a vested stock option represents a right to subscribe to shares, which constitutes a capital asset within the meaning of section 2(14) of the ITA
creating a distinct recognition pathway for deep tech startups
